run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T16:37:36Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is firing because the frontend's ad dependency is unavailable. The single ad replica, pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958, Deployment ad), is Running but not ready, has restartCount 4, and both the last and current container terminations are reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 (16:38:50Z and 16:39:52Z). Deployment ad therefore reports unavailableReplicas 1 with its Available condition False since 16:39:53Z, the ad Service has only a not-ready endpoint, and ad's own server-side oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate fell to 0 by ~16:43. Frontend error spans were 0 until the 16:37:36 sample, then rose to ~3.6 spans/s at peak, and are confined to GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect, while frontend error rates on cart, checkout and product routes remained 0. A pre-incident Jaeger sample confirms the frontend /api/data -> AdService call edge. Cart, checkout, product-catalog and every other otel-demo deployment except ad were checked and are ready/available. The precise trigger of the OOM is not fully proven: the cgroup-recorded peak (~355 MiB) was below the declared 450Mi limit, so the memory accounting between scrapes remains an open gap.

claims.text: frontend error spans (trace status STATUS_CODE_ERROR) were 0 for every sample from 15:37:36 to 16:36:36, first became nonzero at the 16:37:36 sample (0.522 spans/s), peaked at 3.614 spans/s around 16:46:36, and returned to 0 by 16:54:36.

The frontend's error spans are confined to specific operations: GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect. Over the same window, error rates are exactly 0 for grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout.

At 16:37:36 the frontend's per-operation error span rates were 0.122222 for GET, 0.122222 for GET /api/data, 0.122222 for executing api route (pages) /api/data, 0.122222 for the outbound grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds call, and 0.033333 for tcp.connect; the outbound AdService client span carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR while ad's own server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds was recorded under STATUS_CODE_UNSET and ad's only error-labelled span was flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at 0.003704.

Pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 in namespace otel-demo is phase Running while its container ad is not ready with restartCount 4; lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled exitCode 137 finishedAt 2026-11-16T16:38:50Z, and current state.terminated reason OOMKilled exitCode 137 startedAt 16:39:41Z finishedAt 16:39:52Z. Its Ready and ContainersReady conditions are False with reason ContainersNotReady since 16:39:53Z, and its ownerReference is ReplicaSet ad-554b849958.

Deployment ad (namespace otel-demo, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad) has spec.replicas 1, replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1 and unavailableReplicas 1 with no readyReplicas/availableReplicas; its Available condition is status False, reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, message 'Deployment does not have minimum availability.' with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-16T16:39:53Z. Its ad container requests cpu 10m and memory 225Mi, and limits cpu 50m and memory 450Mi.

Kubernetes events for pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 include 23 Warning events with reason BackOff, message 'Back-off restarting failed container ad in pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5_otel-demo(...)', firstTimestamp 2026-11-16T16:36:50Z and lastTimestamp 2026-11-16T16:44:29Z, alongside Normal Created and Started container events with count 6 (15:59:15Z to 16:41:21Z).

The ad Service endpoint has no ready addresses: its only address is in notReadyAddresses (IP 100.96.2.230, targetRef ad-554b849958-l9ft5), while the frontend Service endpoint frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx is a ready address.

Ad's own server-side span rate for operation oteldemo.AdService/GetAds held between 0.740741 and 0.896296 spans/s through 16:38:36, fell to 0.481481 at 16:39:36, 0.066667 at 16:41:36, and was 0 for every sample from 16:43:36 to 16:54:36.

The ad container's memory working set rose monotonically from 333225984 bytes at the 16:12:36 sample to 371867648 bytes from 16:26:36 onward, and container_memory_usage_bytes shows the same profile (333365248 to 372006912 bytes) before the restarts.

The cgroup-recorded peak for the long-lived ad container instance 0660c51865e8... (container_memory_max_usage_bytes) reached 372563968 bytes (~355 MiB), which is below the declared 450Mi limit, and container_memory_failcnt was 0 for every ad container instance sampled; these samples therefore do not show the container crossing its declared memory limit, even though the pod status records OOMKilled terminations.

No node reports memory pressure: all 5 nodes show type MemoryPressure status False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory and message 'kubelet has sufficient memory available', including node i-0d81a0f472ebdc704 (the node hosting the ad pod, allocatable memory 16064772Ki) and node i-0ada79323930d32f6.

All 21 deployments in namespace otel-demo show DESIRED 1, READY 1 and AVAILABLE 1 except ad, which shows READY <none> and UNAVAILABLE 1; this includes frontend, frontend-proxy, flagd, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, payment, product-catalog, recommendation, shipping, postgresql, kafka and valkey-cart.

At 16:45:00 the error-span rate by service was frontend 4.488889 spans/s, frontend-proxy 2.244444 spans/s, fraud-detection 0.003704, recommendation 0.003704, and 0 for accounting, payment and ad; frontend-proxy's errors are on operations 'router frontend egress' (1.118519 spans/s) and 'ingress' (1.125926 spans/s).
The ad container spec has readinessProbe null and livenessProbe null, with resources limits cpu 50m/memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m/memory 225Mi.

The retained current ad container log lines (16:35:22Z to 16:35:41Z) show normal request handling such as 'Targeted ad request received for [books]', 'Targeted ad request received for [travel]' and 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.' shortly before the kills; the filtered search for error/fatal/OOM/memory lines returned no matching line.

A pre-incident Jaeger trace sample (spans starting 16:27:42-16:27:46) shows the path load-generator user_get_ads -> frontend-proxy ingress and 'router frontend egress' -> frontend GET /api/data -> frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds -> ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with rpc.grpc.status_code '0' and http.status_code 200, establishing the frontend /api/data -> AdService call edge from supplied parent references.

The frontend's errors on GET /api/data and its outbound grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, plus the tcp.connect error spans, are caused by the ad pod being OOM-killed and not ready so the ad Service has no ready endpoint. Supporting: first frontend error sample 16:37:36 versus first kill near 16:36 and BackOff events from 16:36:50, matching operation names, ad GetAds server rate falling to 0, and the pre-incident trace confirming the call direction.

frontend-proxy's errors on 'router frontend egress' and 'ingress' are the proxy observing the same failing frontend requests rather than an independent proxy fault: the frontend-proxy Deployment is READY 1/AVAILABLE 1 and its pod has 0 restarts, but incident-window traces are unavailable so a per-request linkage is not verified.

Node-level memory pressure or kubelet eviction was considered as the cause of the ad container restarts and rejected: every node reports MemoryPressure False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory, and the pod's own container status records termination reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 rather than an Evicted pod phase or eviction event.

A frontend code or configuration fault was considered as the origin and rejected as primary: the frontend Deployment is READY 1 and AVAILABLE 1, its pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx has restartCount 0 and ready true with no termination reason, and its errors are 0 on the cart, checkout and product routes it also serves while nonzero only on the /api/data route and its AdService client call.

An ad-side dependency fault such as flagd was considered: ad emitted flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.003704 spans/s at 16:37:36, but the flagd Deployment is READY 1 and AVAILABLE 1, ad's own flagd ResolveBoolean span rates are 0, and ad's retained logs show normal request handling to 16:35:41Z; no ad workload status or event evidence ties flagd to the frontend errors.

Raise the ad container memory limit above the observed growth trajectory (or fix the steady memory growth seen in image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), and add readiness and liveness probes: the pod currently defines neither, the Deployment runs a single replica, and a working set already near 372 MB leaves little headroom under the 450Mi limit.

gaps: No incident-window traces were available: traces_search for frontend over 16:36:00-16:45:00 and traces_search_by_tags with error=true both returned status no_data, and the newest ad trace returned was captured at 16:27:46, so the exact gRPC and HTTP status codes of the failing calls could not be read from traces (views 98204c78-1947-4229-899b-98db1c9b3dc1-t0:f3d80cce-0ef2-47ce-a92e-64cff26cb764 and 34ad640f-c5f7-4698-827f-6d0a838ee2eb-t1:8d55f68d-053d-4e89-9e9a-c5938ad3eb87 report no_data).

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series or label values for service_name frontend in the window (views 022d1610-0839-45b3-8a85-5d6a1244159f-t0:ba45e00b-4bc1-433d-b6a0-5042147b0a8e and 25789c06-e98f-49c8-a626-8042cc809440-t1:95aa70c1-30d5-44fd-9e81-5baaff5ed011 both no_data), so a gRPC status-code breakdown of the frontend's AdService calls is unknown rather than zero.

The alert rule named RequestErrorRate was not found in Prometheus (view 07fefe3a-f872-46e7-b158-89d357b6d9db-t0:6781e34d-61a5-4d68-9b51-e33786d4be0a returned no_data), so the rule expression, threshold and the annotation's reported value 2.622222222222222 are unverified; http_server_request_duration_seconds_count also returned no label values (f246bbeb-96fa-4f1b-b14e-ab90e70ced65-t1:db3b3bbb-c787-4a07-9a2f-5212b7ea6e9a), so the frontend's HTTP 5xx rate is unknown.

The mechanism of the OOM is not proven: cgroup max_usage peaked near 355 MiB against a declared 450Mi limit, samples are 120 s apart, and failcnt was 0; a burst between scrapes or limit accounting differences could explain it but were not verified.

The crashed previous ad container instance's logs were unavailable ('previous terminated container ad ... not found', view 8cbec086-bd42-4c88-b211-f07470b891ca-t0:d157293b-6d0b-415d-866c-de9987c62a8f), the current stream ends at 16:35:41Z, and the retained-log read was incomplete (limit: newest 40 of 2678 lines), so no crash-time stack trace or fatal line is in evidence.

The frontend container returned no stdout/stderr lines in the window (bytes_read 0, view e857c186-ff7f-418f-a0b6-f43dcfdc46e1-t1:89c72074-fbe1-495d-813d-1d21388de18b), so its own application logs could not confirm the client-side failure messages.
Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so whether the ad image, memory limit or replica count changed shortly before the 15:59:12Z pod start could not be checked.
Why the frontend error rate decayed from its 16:45 peak toward 0 while the ad pod remained unavailable (frontend's total span rate also fell in the last samples) is not explained by the evidence.
next_steps: Inspect the ad deployment's rollout history and Helm or manifest values for the memory limit and replica count, since change history was not integrated in this Run.
Review ad application memory behavior or heap profile for the steady growth from ~333 MB to ~372 MB to determine whether the leak is in the application rather than the limit.

Confirm the RequestErrorRate rule definition and the frontend HTTP 5xx rate directly in the alerting Prometheus, which returned no_data for the rule and for http_server_request_duration_seconds_count here.
Verify with incident-window traces (missing here) that the failing frontend spans terminate at the ad Service unavailable endpoint rather than at a proxy timeout.
Plan a follow-up check that ad recovers to a ready endpoint and that frontend /api/data error spans return to 0 before closing the alert.
